scenes.title: Cloud Networking Basics (VPC)
scenes.narration: A Virtual Private Cloud is your own isolated network inside the cloud, where you control IP ranges, subnets, and how traffic flows in and out.

scenes.title: What a VPC Contains
bullets: Subnets divide your network into public and private segments across availability zones.
Route tables and gateways decide how traffic reaches the internet or stays internal.
Security groups and network ACLs act as firewalls controlling allowed traffic.
scenes.narration: A VPC is carved into subnets, some public for internet-facing resources and some private for protected ones. Route tables and gateways determine how packets travel, whether out to the internet or between subnets. Security groups and network ACLs then enforce firewall rules on that traffic.

scenes.title: Public vs. Private Subnets
scenes.narration: A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway, making it the right place for load balancers and bastion hosts. A private subnet has no direct internet path, which is where you keep databases and data processing jobs safe. Separating the two is the foundation of a secure cloud network.

scenes.title: Path to a Private Database
steps: Job runs in a private subnet
Database stays off the public internet
scenes.narration: Consider a data job connecting to a database. Both live in private subnets, and a security group opens only the specific database port between them. The route table keeps that traffic internal, so the database is never exposed to the public internet. This layered approach is standard practice.

scenes.text: A VPC is your private slice of the cloud — keep data stores in private subnets and let security groups grant only the exact ports you need.
scenes.narration: Treat the VPC as your own isolated network. Placing data stores in private subnets and opening only the precise ports required through security groups keeps sensitive systems safely out of public reach.
